lens: recovery truth + identity migration release assurance + public/agent proof surfaces + CANON-019/031/045/048/051
primaryListVerdict: The recovered identity candidate is source- and staging-complete but production-held. The fresh Genius List incorrectly treats service-role REST as DDL/Function authority, and remote post-push evidence reveals a compliance job false-red caused by its own repeated localStorage clearing fixture. S290 must make authority granular, proof durable, promotion dependency-bound, and the remote CI claim honest before any production discussion.

items.title: Repair the compliance test that erases the browser state it is asserting
items.why: S289 browser E2E passed but its compliance job failed; the suite-level claim is therefore not remotely green.
items.premise: Playwright addInitScript runs for later same-origin frames, so localStorage.clear() can execute after the consent click and erase the accepted/declined value.
liveEvidence: GitHub run 30066534572: e2e green, compliance red
Local 5x/2-worker reproduction: consent storage intermittently null
The product click handler writes storage before removing the banner
items.outcome: verification: the exact CI compliance command and a repeated concurrency stress pass both stay green without weakening the product assertion.
items.recipe: Use Playwright's per-test isolated browser context as the clean-state boundary, remove the self-invalidating init script, and assert both dismissal and persisted value under repeated concurrent execution.

L2.recipe: Document fixture isolation and rerun the exact CI command.

L3.recipe: Prove the race is gone across repeated two-worker runs and preserve the storage assertion.

executionLog.note: Exact CI compliance command: 29/29 passed; repeated two-worker consent stress: 40/40 passed.

items.title: Split Supabase REST, management API, SQL migration, and Edge Function authority
items.why: The generic supabase.admin READY signal currently promotes service-role REST into powers it does not possess, producing phantom-actionable work and unsafe release assumptions.
items.premise: The capability map requires only URL plus service-role key; the failed CLI explicitly requires a management token or database deployment credential.
liveEvidence: supabase.admin reports READY 2/2
Supabase management token is not represented by the capability
The migration and function remain undeployed
items.outcome: security + information-finding: one public-safe receipt reports each authority plane separately from harmless live probes, never serializes secrets, and makes partial access impossible to label full control-plane readiness.
items.recipe: Build a gateway-native probe with pure classification tests, read-only REST and management checks, database-credential detection, source hashes, reason codes, and a strict public-safe artifact validator.

L1.recipe: Separate credential presence into four booleans.

L2.recipe: Add harmless provider probes and public reason codes.

L3.recipe: Add negative fixtures, source hashes, secret-field rejection, and build/release integration.

executionLog.note: Gateway-native control-plane probe self-test: 8/8 passed; live REST plane verified HTTP 200 while management, SQL, and Functions remain explicit blockers.

items.title: Render a durable, privacy-safe identity migration receipt before provider E2E exists
items.why: The current handoff contains the evidence only as prose and the migration receipt is incorrectly classified as wholly provider-gated.
items.premise: Issuer, callback host, Worker version, source updates, roles, rollback anchors, and dark E2E states are already independently knowable.
liveEvidence: Canonical staging Worker version 773ec75d-4de8-4246-8f59-582fb061298f
Migration/function source paths exist
Signed-in provider, role, and revocation evidence remains unverified
items.outcome: information-finding: humans and agents can distinguish source-ready, staged, deployed, provider-verified, and production-eligible states without user identifiers, tokens, or fabricated pass states.
items.recipe: Create a small evidence ledger and deterministic renderer that binds source hashes and staging deployment facts while representing every unavailable real-provider proof as explicit honest-dark state.

L2.recipe: Derive source hashes and configuration bindings.

L3.recipe: Validate privacy, evidence consistency, eligibility logic, and release integration.

executionLog.note: Identity receipt self-test: 7/7 passed; receipt binds the final staging Worker version, source hashes, privacy constraints, rollback anchors, and honest-dark provider states.

items.title: Bind production promotion to the identity receipt and control-plane truth
items.why: A human edit could currently flip the hold file to ready even while migrations, provider E2E, or rollback authority remain dark.
items.premise: The workflow gate validates the hold document and manual confirmation but not the independent evidence behind its reasons.
liveEvidence: Four production workflows are correctly dispatch-gated
PRODUCTION_PROMOTION.json is a manually editable state file
Identity/runtime blockers are machine-readable after items 2 and 3
items.outcome: security: promotion cannot become eligible unless the receipt is verified, required authority is ready, reason codes reconcile, staging-first remains true, and the dispatch is explicitly confirmed.
items.recipe: Cross-validate dependency artifacts inside the existing fail-closed gate and release proof, with fixtures proving a cosmetically green hold file cannot bypass dark dependencies.

L2.recipe: Cross-check reason codes and control-plane state.

L3.recipe: Pin bypass attempts in self-tests and every production workflow check.

executionLog.note: Promotion-gate self-test: 11/11 passed, including fake-ready and dependency-bypass attempts.

items.title: Expose identity migration state on the public status surface and agent catalog
items.why: Release posture is technically available but not currently legible as an identity-specific staged-versus-verified signal.
items.premise: The status page already consumes a unified proof manifest and agents.json catalogs public proof feeds.
liveEvidence: Status tiles are DOM-built and honest-dark aware
status-proof bundles public-safe API feeds
agents.json already advertises release-proof
items.outcome: UX + AI discovery: one status tile and two cataloged feeds explain the migration state to humans and agents without extra requests or security-sensitive detail.
items.recipe: Bundle the new receipts into status-proof, add a concise migration tile, and register both artifacts in agents.json with plain-language descriptions.

L3.recipe: Use the one-fetch proof manifest and validate both themes/mobile semantics.

executionLog.note: Both feeds are bundled into status-proof and agents.json; the 390px browser test verifies the staged/held identity tile and 1/4 authority signal without overflow.

items.title: Converge migration, authority, staging, rollback, and promotion into one release proof
items.why: Operators and agents otherwise need to reread handoffs and probe several systems to answer a single question: can this candidate promote?
items.premise: build-release-proof already reconciles candidate and production state and can absorb two bounded public artifacts without new network calls.
liveEvidence: api/release-proof.json is already a cataloged source
Current blockers are only hold reason strings
Status proof eliminates parallel requests by embedding feeds
items.outcome: speed + token/API reduction: one deterministic release proof explains every blocker and eligibility check, lowering repeated provider calls and context reconstruction cost.
items.recipe: Fold compact control-plane and identity summaries into release-proof, add deterministic drift checks, and generate in dependency order before the unified status manifest.

L2.recipe: Preserve reason codes and compact summaries.

L3.recipe: Wire deterministic build order and prove no stale-green combination survives.

executionLog.note: Release proof now derives 15 explicit blockers from identity and authority receipts in deterministic build order; release-proof self-test: 9/9 passed.

items.title: Keep stale ignored Lighthouse artifacts from impersonating a current regression
items.why: The advisory path was surfacing a weeks-old ignored local report after a current-sha Lighthouse workflow had already passed, creating a false release signal.
items.premise: Blocking CI runs --check immediately after collection, while the non-blocking local advisory can encounter an indefinitely old ignored results directory.
liveEvidence: Recovered-SHA Lighthouse workflow 30066534525 is green
Local ignored Lighthouse JSON was 563 hours old
The advisory contract documents exit 0 while strict --check remains blocking
items.outcome: feedback quality: default advisory output only interprets evidence from the last 24 hours, while strict CI semantics remain unchanged and dedicated CI stays authoritative.
items.recipe: Apply a 24-hour age guard only in default advisory mode, preserve strict --check behavior, and pin timestamp/freshness boundaries in pure tests.

L3.recipe: Prove strict mode is unchanged and cover freshness boundaries.

executionLog.note: Lighthouse trend self-test: 23/23 passed; default mode correctly defers stale local artifacts to the current dedicated CI workflow.

items.title: Bind candidate-green staging evidence to the exact deployed build SHA
items.why: Independent release review proved that shell parity alone could preserve candidateReady=true while the S290 status surface and receipts were not deployed to staging.
items.premise: A prior staging release can share the same shell fingerprints as a new candidate even when route content and public proof artifacts differ.
liveEvidence: Staging served build 0251e50 while the local candidate beacon was 396175
The staging /status page lacked both S290 release-truth tiles
The prior release proof still reported stagingCandidateReady=true
items.outcome: release truth: candidate-green is impossible unless the staging build beacon exactly matches the candidate beacon in addition to route, CSP, security-header, and shell checks.
items.recipe: Probe the staging build beacon, persist candidate and deployed SHAs in staging-health, fail candidate evaluation on mismatch, surface the binding in release-proof, and pin the false-green case in both self-tests.

L3.recipe: Bind release proof and add negative tests for inherited stale-green evidence.

executionLog.note: Independent-gate defect root-fixed: staging-parity self-test 16/16 and release-proof self-test 10/10; live proof now correctly holds on staging-build-sha-mismatch.

skipped.reason: Not skipped: retained as an explicit external verification gate. A real Obelisk account ceremony cannot be fabricated by local fixtures.
Rejected: turning an auth/security release gate into streaks or rewards would obscure risk rather than improve the public experience.
Rejected: this problem needs verifiable structured evidence, not probabilistic inference or paid API calls.

honestyLedger.title: S289 remote CI was not all green
honestyLedger.why: The E2E job passed, but the compliance sibling job failed in the same workflow run.

honestyLedger.title: supabase.admin READY means REST only
honestyLedger.why: Its declared keys are URL plus service-role key; neither proves SQL migration nor Function deployment authority.

honestyLedger.title: The receipt can ship before the provider journey
honestyLedger.why: Known evidence should render now while unknown role/revocation proofs remain visibly unverified.

honestyLedger.title: Production remains held
honestyLedger.why: Authorization to implement the migration does not waive the staging, provider, security, or independent release gates.

notes: This plan exhausts the two S289 SIL carries and ships five second-order innovations: dependency-bound promotion, dual-audience proof, release-proof convergence, freshness-aware Lighthouse interpretation, and exact-SHA staging truth. External provider work remains explicit and dark rather than falsely completed.
